newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Texts of statements on Finnish markka ERM entry.
newsitem.headline: Texts of statements on Finnish markka ERM entry.

text.p: Following are the texts of the statements by the EU monetary committee and by the European Commission on the entry of the Finnish markka into the EU Exchange Rate Mechanism.
Monetary Committee Communique

The ministers and central bank governors of the Member States of the European Union, following a decision by the Finnish government to join the exchange rate mechanism of the European Monetary System, have decided by mutual agreement, in a common procedure involving the Commission and the European Monetary Institute, and after consultation with the Monetary Committee, on the terms on which the Finnish markka will participate as of 14 October 1996.

The ministers, the governors, the Commission and the European Monetary Institute warmly welcome the participation of the markka in the exchange rate mechanism, which strengthens the European Monetary System. They congratulated the Finnish authorities on the substantial adjustment already achieved by the Finnish economy, which is reflected in this decision.

The Finnish authorities intend to press on with their successful policies aimed at convergence with the most stable economies of the Community; those policies were most recently set out in the updated convergence programme of September 1996.

The ministers and the central bank governors agreed that the central rate for the markka should be 5.80661 for one Ecu. The bilateral central rates of the markka against the other currencies of the exchange rate mechanism, rounded to six significant figures, will be for 100 markka:
Belgian franc 678.468
Danish krone 125.474
German mark 32.8948
Spanish peseta 2798.41
French franc 110.324
Irish pound 13.6433
Luxembourg franc 678.468
Dutch guilder 37.0636
Austrian schilling 231.431
Portuguese escudo 3371.88

The current fluctuation margins of 15 percent will be observed around these bilateral central rates. All other bilateral central rates and intervention rates within the exchange rate mechanism remain unchanged. The decision on the markka's participation has no agri-monetary consequences.
The compulsory intervention points in the exchange rate mechanism will be communicated by the central banks in time for the opening of foreign exchange markets on 14 October 1996.
European Commission Statement
President Jacques Santer and Yves-Thibault de Silguy, European Commissioner responsible for economic, monetary and financial affairs, made the following declaration in the name of the Commission:

The Commission welcomes the entry of the Finnish markka in the exchange rate mechansim of the European Monetary System (EMS). The enlargement of the mechanism to include a new currency is a new very positive signal on the way to the realisation of the euro. Since the monetary fluctuations of spring 1995, great stability has returned to the European Monetary System. The participation of a new member in the mechanism reinforces its credibility and monetary stability in Europe.

The chosen central rate of 5.80661 markkas to the Ecu is fully in line with Finland's good economic performance and with market sentiment. The rapid consolidation of public finances and the absence of inflation are positive factors for durable stability of the markka within the system.

The decision of the Finnish authorities is further evidence of their commitment to participate in the euro. The Commission welcomes the determination of all member states to take the necessary action to ensure that a significant number of countries meet the necessary conditions to participate in the euro from 1 January, 1999.

The decision comes in the context of a more favourable economic situation in the Union. Member states are making real efforts to improve their budgetary situations. There are no inflationary pressures. Both long and short term rates have fallen considerably, in particular in recent months, and spreads have significantly narrowed. All these factors are favourable for growth and employment in Europe. ENDS TEXTS
